Expected: Authorized playback works without unrelated fallback media or browser exceptions. Do not infer watched progress solely from an open iframe.
Observed: Actual protected Bunny media decoded and time advanced in desktop Chrome. Pause, seek to 5 seconds, volume 0.4, fullscreen entry/exit, and course reload/player reopening passed. Playback state was measured on the provider video element. an open iframe alone was not treated as playback.

Expected: App does not issue playable private content to unauthorized viewers. A copied valid bearer embed URL may work until expiry. that alone does not prove the application access check failed.
Observed: With a real encoded private video present, anonymous/private context, unenrolled learner and C2-only enrollment received no playback URL. Anonymous and unenrolled lesson clicks did not render a Bunny player. Copied bearer URL behavior until expiry is not claimed to be identity-bound.

Expected: Tampered and expired signed URLs cannot begin fresh playback. authorized app navigation can obtain a new valid URL. Do not publish the signed URL as evidence.
Observed: Bunny rejected the tampered token. A 25-second token from the application signer played before expiry. Reopening the exact expired link in the previously used browser advanced playback four seconds after expiry. A clean browser, a fresh request with a unique query and a never-used token 600 seconds past expiry each showed a denial. A browser cache or retained provider state may contribute. The precise cause is unconfirmed.
Evidence source: Live token tests and expiry diagnosis

Expected: Provider protection is active during working playback and no app MP4 fallback is exposed. Document only observed evidence. watermark, hidden download buttons, or iframe use alone do not prove encryption or prevent screen recording. External YouTube/Vimeo/public-file links are outside Bunny DRM coverage.
Observed: Protected media played on desktop Chrome and a 390px Android Chrome emulation. no MP4 fallback response was observed. Provider network observations are saved. A physical mobile browser and independent encryption certification were not available, so this case remains blocked rather than overstating emulation as real-device coverage.

Expected: Private resource requires C1 access. preview follows its configured policy. missing files do not open fabricated PDFs. Direct public-storage URLs have a known separate protection limitation.
Observed: Resource entitlement and genuine PDF byte-delivery checks passed. After a bounded rendering wait, readable PDF page text was not demonstrated in headless Chrome. inspect pdf-viewer.png and confirm in a supported real browser. Diagnostic fetches: browserBefore:204, browserAfter:204, browserCacheBusted:204, browserRange:204. Direct unauthenticated file retrieval also returned the PDF, so the public underlying URL has no enrollment gate. No readable-viewer pass is inferred from the iframe or watermark.
